question: A 23-year-old man presents with fatigue and increased daytime somnolence. He says his symptoms began gradually 6 months ago and have progressively worsened and have begun to interfere with his job as a computer programmer. He is also bothered by episodes of paralysis upon waking from naps and reports visual hallucinations when falling asleep at night. He has been under the care of another physician for the past several months, who prescribed him the standard pharmacotherapy for his most likely diagnosis. However, he has continued to experience an incomplete remission of symptoms and has been advised against increasing the dose of his current medication because of an increased risk of adverse effects. Which of the following side effects is most closely associated with the standard drug treatment for this patient’s most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Excessive daytime somnolence -> episodes of paralysis upon waking from naps -> visual hallucinations when falling asleep at night -> possible narcolepsy diagnosis -> pharmacotherapy for narcolepsy -> side effect profile assessment -> Weight gain and metabolic syndrome -> 80%

CHAIN: Fatigue and increased daytime somnolence -> interference with job performance -> seeking medical care -> standard pharmacotherapy for narcolepsy -> side effect profile assessment -> Weight gain and metabolic syndrome -> 85%
analysis: The patient's symptoms of fatigue, increased daytime somnolence, episodes of paralysis upon waking, and visual hallucinations when falling asleep are suggestive of narcolepsy. The standard pharmacotherapy for narcolepsy includes stimulant medications like modafinil or methylphenidate. Weight gain and metabolic syndrome are commonly associated with these stimulant medications used to treat narcolepsy.
